title: Winter Swimming in Berlin - FAQ
subtitle: Where winter swimming is allowed in Berlin, how cold the lakes get and how to start safely.

items.q: Is winter swimming allowed in Berlin?
items.a: Yes, in the waters that are legal in summer. **The bathing rules have no season attached;** the 15 May to 15 September season only covers water testing. The Spree, the canals and the Havel between Eiswerder and Schildhorn stay banned all year.

items.q: Where can I swim in a Berlin lake in winter?
items.a: Plan around lakes listed as a whole or with free shores: **Schlachtensee, Krumme Lanke, Wannsee and the Unterhavel beaches, the Müggelsee, Groß Glienicker See, Tegeler See and the Dahme lakes.** At the Orankesee, Weißer See and Plötzensee only the lido is bathing water, and the lidos are closed.

items.q: How cold do Berlin lakes get in winter?
items.a: Last winter most gauges fell **under 10 °C between late October and mid November and under 4 °C by late December.** The coldest readings came in January and early February, close to 0 °C, and the water was back above 8 °C only in mid to late March.

items.q: Can I join the Berliner Seehunde?
items.a: The club swims at the Orankesee lido every Sunday at 10:00 from mid September to the end of April, but **its list for trial swims is closed at the moment** and the Sunday swims are for members. The public Eisfasching in January is the easiest way to see it.

items.q: Is there a public ice swim in Berlin?
items.a: Yes. The **Großes Eisbaden at Seebad Friedrichshagen** on the Müggelsee takes place on 17 January 2027, €15 in presale or €17 at the gate. The Seehunde also hold their Eisfasching at Strandbad Orankesee on the second Saturday of January.

items.q: How long should I stay in cold water as a beginner?
items.a: **A few seconds up to one minute.** Even experienced swimmers stay no longer than one minute per degree of water temperature. Walk in slowly, never jump, and never swim alone.

items.q: When is it safe to walk on a frozen Berlin lake?
items.a: DLRG Berlin says **only at 15 cm of ice on a lake and 20 cm on a river,** never alone and never on the first cold days. If someone falls through, call 112 and reach them from the shore.
